title: Angles on parallel lines
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point covers all three rules (corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles), but the closest bank points each teach only part of it: one covers corresponding and alternate angles and the other covers co-interior angles, so neither matches the full point.

draft.title: Angles on parallel lines
card: A transversal is a line that crosses two or more other lines. When it crosses two parallel lines, it makes eight angles, and some of them are linked.
angles in matching positions at the two crossings, such as both above the line and on the right of the transversal. They are equal. They form an F shape.
angles between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. They are equal. They form a Z shape.

angles between the parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal. They add to \(180^{\circ}\), so each is \(180^{\circ}\) minus the other. Example: if one is \(70^{\circ}\), the other is \(180^{\circ} - 70^{\circ} = 110^{\circ}\). They form a C shape.
draft.remember: Parallel lines: F is equal, Z is equal, C adds to \(180^{\circ}\).

a.q: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One co-interior angle is \(65^{\circ}\). What is the other co-interior angle?
a.why: Co-interior angles add to \(180^{\circ}\), so the other angle is \(180^{\circ} - 65^{\circ} = 115^{\circ}\). \(65^{\circ}\) is tempting, but that is the answer for equal angles such as alternate or corresponding ones.
a.clue: Co-interior angles are the C shape. Do they add up or match?

b.q: Two parallel fences are crossed by a path. An angle between the fences is \(112^{\circ}\). On the opposite side of the path, the angle between the fences that forms a Z shape with it is called \(x\). What is \(x\)?
b.why: The Z shape means the two are alternate angles, and alternate angles are equal, so \(x = 112^{\circ}\). \(68^{\circ}\) is tempting, but that is what you get by treating them as co-interior angles and subtracting from \(180^{\circ}\).
b.clue: A Z shape names one type of angle pair. Is it equal or does it add to 180?

wants.brief: Two horizontal parallel lines marked with arrows, crossed by a slanted transversal. Label the eight angles with letters a to h. Colour one pair of corresponding angles, one pair of alternate angles and one pair of co-interior angles, each with a matching F, Z or C shape traced beside it.
wants.why: Seeing the F, Z and C shapes on one diagram helps students spot each type of angle pair.
